name: Syringomyelia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiological and clinical diagnostic criteria for syringomyelia

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic neurological symptoms such as dissociated sensory loss and segmental weakness
MRI demonstrating fluid-filled cystic cavity (syrinx) within the spinal cord
Exclusion of other causes of spinal cord cystic lesions or myelopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical symptoms plus MRI evidence of syrinx within the spinal cord
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on MRI findings correlated with clinical presentation.

normal touch but no pain sensation

localized muscle weakness and shrinkage

pathognomonic.symptomName: Syrinx cavity visible on spinal cord MRI

spinal cord cyst on imaging
central spinal cord cavity seen on scan
nerve pain in specific skin areas
burning or shooting pain in dermatomes
neuropathic pain along nerve distribution
stiff and tight limbs
muscle spasticity in arms and legs
limb muscle stiffness and spasms

common.symptomName: Loss of deep tendon reflexes at affected segments
searchTerms: absent reflexes in affected areas
loss of knee or ankle reflexes

laboratory: Generally normal; CSF analysis may be performed to exclude infection or inflammation
imaging: MRI of the spinal cord showing fluid-filled syrinx cavity
MRI brain may show associated Chiari malformation
genetic: No specific genetic markers; may be associated with congenital malformations
other: Electromyography may show denervation in affected muscles

distinguishingFeatures: Demyelinating plaques on MRI rather than cystic syrinx
Progressive neurological deficits without dissociated sensory loss pattern
Possible systemic symptoms depending on tumor type

redFlags: Sudden onset of bladder or bowel dysfunction
Acute respiratory distress in high cervical syringomyelia
references: Kumar N. Syringomyelia: Pathogenesis, Clinical Features, and Management. Neurol Clin. 2019;37(3):491-507.
